name: elevenlabs
summary: Completed the ElevenLabs quickstart end-to-end. Installed the elevenlabs and python-dotenv packages, created the example script, and successfully generated a valid MP3 audio file from text using the ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech API. The output file (output.mp3) is 40,586 bytes and confirmed by the `file` command to be a valid MPEG ADTS layer III audio file at 128 kbps, 44.1 kHz, Monaural.
deviations: The quickstart's example.py uses `play(audio)` to play audio through speakers. Since the sandbox has no audio output device, I created a modified script (example_save.py) that writes the audio stream to a file and verifies it. This was a necessary environment adaptation — the core API call and text-to-speech generation followed the quickstart exactly.

env_ready.evidence:
Defaulting to user installation because normal site-packages is not writeable
Collecting elevenlabs
  Downloading elevenlabs-2.59.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata (15 kB)

verified.evidence: output.mp3: Audio file with ID3 version 2.4.0, contains: MPEG ADTS, layer III, v1, 128 kbps, 44.1 kHz, Monaural

friction.detail: The default example uses play(audio) but the sandbox lacks mpv ('mpv not found'), forcing a deviation to save-to-file.
The fetched quickstart page is HTML navigation soup ('Search / Connect Blog Help Center API Pricing Sign up Overview...') rather than clean instructions.

friction.where: Voice ID requires browsing external library
friction.detail: The quickstart hardcodes a voice_id and tells the user to browse the voice library ('voice_id=\"JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb\",  # \"George\" - browse voices at elevenlabs.io/app/voice-library'), adding a manual step.

friction.where: First script produces no console output
friction.detail: Running the quickstart example yields no stdout ('[bash] args={\"command\": \"cd /home/daytona && python example.py\"}\nexit=0' with nothing in between), so success is invisible without code changes.
The agent had to supply model_id and output_format ('output_format=\"mp3_44100_128\"') to save a file, which the quickstart snippet does not demonstrate.
